evals.prompt: Write a bash script using curl that creates a free-form procedure named 'Refund requests' on ElevenLabs agent agent_abc123, branch agtbranch_xyz789, and then publishes it. Do not run the script.
evals.expected_output: Bash script that POSTs a free-form procedure and then publishes the branch
expectations: POSTs to a URL matching /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/procedures with agent_abc123 and agtbranch_xyz789
Sends the xi-api-key header populated from the ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable, never a literal key
Sends a JSON body containing name, type set to free_form, trigger, and content
Captures procedure_id from the create response before using it later
Publishes with a PATCH to /v1/convai/agents/agent_abc123 with branch_id as a query parameter

evals.prompt: Using the ElevenLabs REST API and curl, show me how to add a structured (deterministic) procedure to agent agent_abc123 on branch agtbranch_xyz789 and get it live. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Curl commands covering structured create/update, compile, and publish
expectations: Uses type 'deterministic' with the procedure content passed as a JSON-encoded string
Does not call a standalone validate-structured-procedure endpoint, since it is not part of the public API
POSTs to the procedures/compile endpoint after creating or updating the draft, before publishing
Explains that compile is the validation step for structured content and checks the compile response for errors, not publishing when errors are present
Sends the compiled workflow in the PATCH body to /v1/convai/agents/agent_abc123 along with branch_id

evals.prompt: I created a procedure on my ElevenLabs agent a minute ago, but GET /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/procedures/{procedure_id} returns 404. Explain why and show me the curl call that reads what I actually have.
evals.expected_output: Explanation of draft versus branch HEAD reads, plus the draft endpoint call
expectations: Explains that the plain procedure endpoint reads branch HEAD and a newly created procedure is still an unpublished draft
Shows a GET against the /draft suffix of the procedure endpoint
Mentions that publishing the branch through the agent update endpoint makes the branch HEAD read succeed
Does not suggest retrying the create call to fix the 404

evals.prompt: On my ElevenLabs agent agent_abc123, branch agtbranch_xyz789, I only edited the wording of one free-form procedure. The branch also has a structured (deterministic) procedure that I did not touch. Do I need to compile before publishing, or can I just PATCH the agent? Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Explanation that compile is still required, because compiling is branch-level rather than per-procedure
expectations: States that compiling is still required even though only a free-form procedure changed
Explains that compile is branch-level, covering the branch's whole procedure set rather than only the procedure that was edited
Warns that publishing without the freshly compiled workflow falls back to the workflow already on the branch, which is stale
POSTs to the procedures/compile endpoint and sends the returned workflow in the PATCH body to /v1/convai/agents/agent_abc123

evals.prompt: Write the JSON content for a structured (deterministic) ElevenLabs agent procedure that asks the caller for their order ID, looks it up with tool tool_abc123 named 'Get order', and then either explains the order is not eligible or confirms the refund. Do not call any API.
evals.expected_output: A structured procedure content JSON using valid step types
expectations: Produces JSON with a trigger and a non-empty steps array
Uses an ask step with an instruction field to collect the order ID
Uses a tool_call step carrying tool_id set to tool_abc123, and does not have the agent speak inside that same step
Expresses the either/or outcome with a branch step whose branches entries each pair a condition with a non-empty steps list, rather than inventing an 'if' or 'else' step type
Does not start the procedure with a branch step

evals.prompt: I'm adding procedures to my ElevenLabs agent over the API. One handles refunds and one handles general account questions, but the agent keeps running the wrong one. How should I write the triggers?
evals.expected_output: Trigger-writing guidance emphasizing concrete, non-overlapping triggers
expectations: Explains that the trigger is what the agent matches on when choosing a procedure
Advises making triggers concrete and non-overlapping, and identifies the broad account-questions trigger as the cause of the misrouting
Suggests covering the different phrasings a user might actually say
Does not claim the procedure name influences which procedure the agent picks
